After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Nileme give way! Vanguard forces of SurahaTawantin storm the royal seat of Nileme, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
Fires of Beltane: People of Dun Rachys wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Dun Rachys.
Festival of Lanterns for the Dead: Families in Neka set out lamps and food for their dead at Neka.
Envoys from Drinvopatna and Ranvuzh exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Neither camp can break the front: envoys sign a mutual cessation of hostilities, ending the Yefọ Succession War (4 years) in an uneasy truce.
Shesehe of Chia comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Dynastic extinction strikes Chia: Cholime dies heirless (a wasting sickness). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Wododi claims the vacant crown.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Dun Rachys seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of Micia! The people inaugurate the Free Union of Corgenwy under the stewardship of Hedhensara.
Hedhensara is acclaimed ruler of Free Union of Corgenwy.

Outraged by treason, the crown of Military Junta of Micia mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Free Union of Corgenwy. The War of the Corgenwy Crown begins in fire and iron.
Insurrection flares in Duzhpop! Declaring their liberties inviolable, the populace casts off the yoke of Tatshia and rallies beneath the banner of Sheszhez, establishing the Iron Dominion of Nigvuzh.
Sheszhez is acclaimed ruler of Iron Dominion of Nigvuzh.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Commune of Tatshia dispatches punitive legions to subdue Iron Dominion of Nigvuzh. The bitter Nigvuzh Campaign is underway.
A blazing crimson comet arcs across the night skies above Rifdig; court astrologers dispute whether it foretells glorious conquest or catastrophic ruin.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Timpid storm the government palace in Mudshuy! The faction seizes control, establishing the Principality of Mudshuy.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Vona storm the government palace in Dengencac! The faction seizes control, establishing the Holy See of Dengencac.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Ziucheng! Rua seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Grand Duchy of Ziucheng!
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Nii! Kiu seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the High Realm of Nii!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Nupe are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Celsyd!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Celsyd detonate powder stores in Brona, gutting frontline regiments!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Cornadwy stir mutiny among garrison troops in SurahaTawantin!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Batsvyz embarks upon the Liberation of the Captive Sage in Nichome! Batsvyz gathers scouts and infiltrates the frontier redoubts near Nichome to pinpoint the captive's cell.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Sanurishu pave the Buazhou-Vygmyd Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Buazhou and Vygmyd (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Mudshuy pave the Vegchegorod-Muwini Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Vegchegorod and Muwini (+trade, +stability).
The Pohvekhkand–Suvlut Rustline is rebuilt: Dengencac relays the track, and trains run again.
The Gadqeyguq–Dizqey Rustline of Zogdar reaches Choglalibela: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
The Degban–Llan-men Rustline of Begvedhys reaches Deshmul: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).
RUINOUS GIFT: Luxuria the Gilded Prince intoxicates the high courts of Hutokushima with exquisite hedonism! Opulence surges alongside reckless decadence (+40 gold, -10 stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Khorvath the Blood Lord floods the warriors of Zhevzhed with bloodthirsty slaughter! Mortal legions butcher foes with demonic savagery (+25% army power, -8 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Undina of the Silver Basin purifies the sacred rivers of Khaoling! Abundant fish and unhindered river trade enrich the townships (+30 gold, +12 stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Omnipotis the Sovereign Architect manifests the Sovereign Mandate in Corgenwy! Incorruptible celestial magistrates codify sacred law, crushing unrest (+20 stability, +15 gold).
Koa, bald and half-blind from the storms, preaches in Payang that the sky will clear for those who stop digging.

Timpid of Mudshuy comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
Rua of Ziucheng comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Kiu of Nii comes to the throne bent on knowledge.
Miffaha conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Ashen Labyrinth) using tactic (score 8 vs DC 8). Defeated Bael. Promoted to F-Rank!
Baznagduda survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 5 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
Longships of Bopheim return to Bopheim laden with far-off silver.
Ze'olyat Beyond dissolves the Hermits of Mother of Rebrurdyn and seizes its houses.
Soldiers scatter a call to break the lords' hold in Kakpob; Miqeme keeps manorial fiefs by force.
A great fungal bloom carpets the caverns of Shahsij; spore-bread and lamp-moss for all.
A great fungal bloom carpets the caverns of Konmat around Konmat; spore-bread and lamp-moss for all.
A royal wedding joins Yipweybije of Mibbu and Welbotyeme of Bucha; the two realms are united under one crown.
Tunöstan squeezes the shaft-tolls of Luswur; the miners of Begvedhys mutter beneath the stone.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Lishliqar bars the shaft to Melneb, and the tithe-collectors of Dengencac are turned back at the lamps of Shizhijabad.
Begvedhys squeezes the shaft-tolls of Haslishquf; the miners of Shizhijabad mutter beneath the stone.
Hutokushima squeezes the shaft-tolls of Bolabad; the miners of Beta Dewo mutter beneath the stone.
Rain-soaked slopes slide into the valley of Men, burying the lower village of Begvedhys.
The Yefọ Succession War is known as the Great Reckoning among the Sarnilnyl, and as the Plunder among the Wepe.
Night of Pomegranates: The longest night in Ranvuzh is spent by firelight in Podderstan, with stories and gifts.
Ze'olyat Beyond's invasion through the Weeping Door into Dekoru was repulsed at O'ahuaghyel.

monsters.name: The Frost-Maned Guardian
monsters.lore: A colossal pale tiger of snow-clad ridges, silent as autumn wind, that warbands speak of only in whispers.

monsters.name: Abyssal Terror
monsters.lore: A colossal multi-tentacled sea monster capable of pulling entire armadas down into the black abyss.

monsters.name: The Great Calydonian Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: Behemoth the Earth-Shaker
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: The Celestial Raptor
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: The Radiant Sovereign
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: Winterfang
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: Tepegöz the One-Eyed
monsters.lore: A one-eyed giant of the steppe epics, slain only by a hero clever enough to blind him.

monsters.name: The Each-uisge of the Loch
monsters.lore: A water horse that lets riders mount, then plunges into the loch with them stuck fast.

monsters.name: Kappa of the Reed Pools
monsters.lore: A water imp with a dish of water on its head; bow to it, and courtesy forces it to bow back and spill its strength.

monsters.name: Bakunawa the Moon-Eater
monsters.lore: A great sea serpent that rises to swallow the moon; villagers drive it back by banging pots and pans until it spits the moon out.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

events.text: Loflaz Outlaw Lair raided trade routes near Loflaz, siphoning 34 gold into their hoard.
U'yghzuaxa of Ze'olziez comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Ty'yzteara of Qe'axliux comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
Vangema of Kilumopu comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Tlischala III of Mayliltlan lets go of the aim for a lasting legacy.
Tuperapa of Tinangama comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Niwulu of Linosobebu comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Kamkomtlen of Kawtlit secures the line, with Nekmiwa grown to take the crown.
Te'oxghyit conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Clockwork Chasm) using assault (score 34 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Ba'joi survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 8 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
Scribes of Ba'sakotoo write bark-paper codices at Ba'sakotoo, recording the kings in glyphs.
Panuwonui suppresses the last houses of the Sworn Brothers of Oak Grove of Ryvu; its brothers scatter or go underground.
O'irzaet crushes the cause of emancipation; its leaders hang and the golems are bound tighter.
The old commons no longer suffice for so wide a realm as Papmil; it turns to free guilds.
Something vast stirs in the lightless depths beneath Qasr Fatsiq; the deep wardens double their watch.
Something vast stirs in the lightless depths beneath O'irzaet; the deep wardens double their watch.
A cold upwelling chills the domes of Nopsum'u; kelp farms wither and the reefs bleach.
The tiny Free Commonwealth of Mitegeny seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Linosobebu.
A whirlwind walks across the plains of Hetonoruhybo in late spring and through the heart of Hetonoruhybo, scattering roofs like leaves.
The Hywo Campaign is known as the Holy Defence in Linosobebu, and as the Heretics' War in Hywo.
The Petpan–Tlepco Rustline is cut: soldiers of Feba tear up the salvage rail track and the trains stop.
The Tlitnet–Feba Rustline is cut: soldiers of Feba tear up the salvage rail track and the trains stop.
Ballgame of the Hero Twins: Warriors of Bo'seha parade and wrestle in the squares of We'ji to honour the old victories.
Flames engulf the towers of Ba'sakotoo! Soldiers of Bizuwu force the inner courtyards of Ba'sakotoo's capital; the royal garrison breaks, and the seat of power falls.
Envoys from Papmil and Kawmaltlan exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Losfalma of Lofzamin comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
The bells of Lofzamin toll for the passing of Raglsubbef Open-Hand Hazhyvom (a fall from a horse). The youth Losfalma ascends the throne under a regency council.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Declaring citizen liberty inviolable, the populace of Kil-rebule casts out imperial governors! Renouncing allegiance to No'ajaw, Guva proclaims the sovereign Free Commonwealth of Febia.
Guva is acclaimed ruler of Free Commonwealth of Febia.

The Invasion of Ruhengahu is known as the Liberation among the Buhyrynodybu, and as the Betrayal among the Pomome.
The banners of No'ajaw are raised over Numowukawa as victorious cohorts march in, ending Cyryva's dominion over the district.
Blossom-Viewing: People of Kowo wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Kowo.
Fires of Beltane: People of Gilia wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Byty.
Feast of Flowers: People of Wetlnow wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Tlitnet.
A catastrophic blow to Chommom: legions of Lenonila overrun the citadel of Chommom, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Border War of Sidywy ends in mutual exhaustion after 2 years; borders return to former lines.
An ancient sovereign power falls to dust: High Realm of Chommom is extinguished. Royal archives smolder, and Wichpama Panpoch flees into obscurity.
The Border War of Chommom reaches its conclusion after 1 year of bloodshed: Lenonila triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
Ambition stirs in the courts of Grand Duchy of Eytughy, which openly claims dominion over Free City of Figvar. The holdfast braces as the Border War of Figvar erupts.

With swords drawn and ancient pacts invoked, Holy See of Chimwamhuacan marches against Principality of Pu'jetk'in. The Hundred Days War of Pu'jetk'in begins. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of No'ajaw rally to Pu'jetk'in's side.
Through stubborn resolve, No'ajaw & Vuwo shatter the enemy offensive. The Great Crusade against No'ajaw ends after 4 years with the defenders holding firm.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Cyryva Succession War ends in mutual exhaustion after 1 year; borders return to former lines.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Border War of Figvar ends in mutual exhaustion after less than a year; borders return to former lines.
Sotywa of Relo turns from the old cause toward a lasting legacy.
In Relo, Ele the Fair Nubu departs this life, succumbing to a wasting sickness. The child Sotywa (age 9) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.
Okhoxtu of Izyloth turns from the old cause toward glory.
A perilous interregnum grips Izyloth following the heirless death of Ytkuxyixy (old age). Retainers of House Uxghihkyghy storm the assembly and usurp the crown.
Galled by heavy cap levies and distant decrees, the citizens of Ba'sakotoo cast out their toll-men! Renouncing all allegiance to Bizuwu, Ba'ki proclaims the sovereign Stratocracy of Ju'misouto.
Ba'ki is acclaimed ruler of Stratocracy of Ju'misouto.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Merchant League of Bizuwu marches swiftly upon Stratocracy of Ju'misouto. The drums of the Great Bizuwu War echo across the provinces.
Insurrection flares in Yekekawa! Declaring their liberties inviolable, the populace casts off the yoke of Cyryva and rallies beneath the banner of Nememi, establishing the High Realm of Ninoki.
Nememi is acclaimed ruler of High Realm of Ninoki.
Outraged by treason, the crown of Merchant League of Cyryva mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in High Realm of Ninoki. The Ninoki Campaign begins in fire and iron.

REPUBLICAN REVOLT: Weary of monarchical tyranny, the burghers and civic guilds of Kilumopu take up arms for freedom! Seceding from Lohyapy, they hoist republican banners beneath Luvanu to establish the Republic of Kilumopu.
Luvanu is acclaimed ruler of Republic of Kilumopu.

Outraged by treason, the crown of Free Trading Cities of Lohyapy mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in Republic of Kilumopu. The Border War of Kilumopu begins in fire and iron.
Dust storms and blighted crops leave Wuberadata on half-rations; canned stores are guarded at gunpoint.
Gume opens the royal canned stores of Wuberadata; bread is carted to every village and the people bless the crown.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Luwia! Wibylu seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Kingdom of Luwia!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Iyghezy as a mass uprising topples the throne of Principality of Iyghezy! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Ughqughtu proclaims the sovereign Popular Commonwealth of Iyghezy!
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Yqqeghxozy storm the government palace in Ihqixy! The faction seizes control, establishing the Council of Ingenuity of Ihqixy.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Linosobebu as a mass uprising topples the throne of Empire of Linosobebu! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Heka proclaims the sovereign United Provinces of Linosobebu!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from We'tatun divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Nenubonape!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of We'tatun are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Nenubonape!
QUEST COMPLETED: Delve into the Primeval Foundry in Te'axgyeh! Fugi returns triumphant from Te'axgyeh, having uncovered forgotten secrets and winning Immortal Renown!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Ko'sipe embarks upon the Raid on the Shadow Keep in Kosone! Ko'sipe gathers scouts and infiltrates the frontier redoubts near Kosone to pinpoint the captive's cell.

The Te Tuno–Mukika Rustline of Fipopenui reaches Fumowitu: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).

The vault-born Bowylu clears the tunnels under Limegy of mutant swarms; the people call them Warden.
The Half-Lifed gathers around a still-humming reactor ruin near Fofefe, praying to the glow.
Jo'sa, bald and half-blind from the storms, preaches in Ix-po'chu that the sky will clear for those who stop digging.
A scrap-prophet, Xi'uroox, wanders into Qeutzaagh with a crackling radio and a message from the Old Voice.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Te Nitiwi (Mewosuteku).

Borne on the winds, Al-wuh now drifts above the open sea.

The Great Crusade against No'ajaw is known as the Usurpation in Palu, and as the Reclamation in No'ajaw.
Masquerade Season: People of Nenubonape wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Fenofe.
After 31 months, the River Purging is gone; Fipopenui counts the empty houses.
Ballgame of the Hero Twins: Warriors of Pana parade and wrestle in the squares of Bima to honour the old victories.
The walls of Kilumopu crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Lohyapy breach the defenses of Kilumopu's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
Festival of Lanterns for the Dead: Families in Numikoku set out lamps and food for their dead at Tokemuwomi.
Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Commercial Union of Tikimoto mobilizes its hosts against Commune of Kowo. Banners unfurl for the Kowo Campaign.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the Border War of Kilumopu after 1 year. With frontiers redrawn, Lohyapy dictate terms to the vanquished.
Humbled, Republic of Kilumopu bends the knee and becomes a vassal of Lohyapy, paying yearly tribute.
To'tape of Bo'seha comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
The death of Wo'e Se'muna (poison) leaves Bo'seha without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Wo'bi seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.
Oqzozh of Ukyutt comes to the throne bent on wealth.
In Ukyutt, Yqhuqy the Grasping Uqxyhzittoqy departs this life, succumbing to old age. The child Oqzozh (age 13) is crowned beneath a wary council of regents.
Ytkukhohqu of Iyghezy takes up the cause of knowledge.
The death of Ughqughtu Eqteyh (old age) leaves Iyghezy without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Oztizhyyh seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal cap levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Waptlal rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Bizuwu, they establish the Commune of Waptlal with Kewpawmipa leading the commune.
Kewpawmipa is acclaimed ruler of Commune of Waptlal.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Merchant League of Bizuwu marches swiftly upon Commune of Waptlal. The drums of the Invasion of Waptlal echo across the provinces.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Dirynomore seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of Sidywy! The people inaugurate the Commune of Dirynomore under the stewardship of Mesyvy.
Mesyvy is acclaimed ruler of Commune of Dirynomore.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Trade Federation of Sidywy dispatches punitive legions to subdue Commune of Dirynomore. The bitter War of Sidywy is underway.
Dust storms and blighted crops leave Lushyujdas on half-rations; canned stores are guarded at gunpoint.
The lords of Lushyujdas hoard grain and sell it dear; Raqtufsita grows richer as the villages empty.
Kolu (Master Artisan) composes an immortal ballad that brings tears to commoners and kings alike in Fofefe.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Pejoku! Tala seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Stratocracy of Pejoku!

COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Ze'olziez stir mutiny among garrison troops in Bizuwu!

House Lavari of Ruhengahu and House Nupuvu of Rulika were joined in royal marriage.
Napama of Linosobebu comes to the throne bent on a lasting legacy.
Nemu of Gilia keeps the holdfast whole through 20 hard years.
Yowe conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Clockwork Chasm) using assault (score 27 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Potlnaw survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 10 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
Canoes from every island of Fumome race into the lagoon at Te Ruti.
The Tidal Players of Fekhbeffan takes shape in O'irzaet: players who stage the old tales in a new manner.
Dynuwo mac Hahena founds the Charter League in Sasofugoce; its pamphlets call for legal reform across Vuwo.
Victorious in the field, Linosobebu forces free guilds upon the beaten Rutinilitani.
Under the hand of O'irzaet, Iyghezy gives up clan commons for thralldom.
The tiny United Provinces of Kawtlit seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Nenubonape.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Chu'jeha bars the shaft to Fumome, and the tithe-collectors of Fipopenui are turned back at the lamps of Ze'olyat.

TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Loflaz bars the shaft to Tlatlwatltit, and the tithe-collectors of Pachsaw are turned back at the lamps of Lofzamin.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Hoizziiq bars the shaft to Kakfuyfus, and the tithe-collectors of Lohyapy are turned back at the lamps of Eytughy.
Lohyapy squeezes the shaft-tolls of Loolruyx; the miners of Ze'olyat mutter beneath the stone.
Nopsum'u raises its port toll at Popache; the harbour-masters of Pejoku protest.
A twisting storm drops from a green sky onto Nonga, tearing a mile-long scar through houses and barns.
A mountainside gives way above Kocha; houses, a road and a mill are buried in a single roar of mud and stone.
The War of the Vuwo Crown is known as the Holy Defence among the Vasavo, and as the Heretics' War among the Nunetu.
The Invasion of Rutinilitani is known as the Vindication among the Buhyrynodybu, and as the Aggression among the Pomome.
Ballgame Festival: Warriors of Mayliltlan parade and wrestle in the squares of Nititlan to honour the old victories.
Lammas Gathering: Granaries of Sidywy are opened at Kil-luwe; the whole town eats until dusk.

Ambition stirs in the courts of Sacred Order of Vuwo, which openly claims dominion over Workers' Federation of Nipi. The holdfast braces as the War of Vuwo erupts. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of So'chekab, No'ajaw rally to Nipi's side.

Ambition stirs in the courts of Principality of Linosobebu, which openly claims dominion over Divine Realm of Kilumopu. The holdfast braces as the Great Linosobebu War erupts. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Lohyapy rally to Kilumopu's side.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Tikimoto seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of Luwia! The people inaugurate the People's Republic of Rabehodi under the stewardship of Gabu.
Gabu is acclaimed ruler of People's Republic of Rabehodi.
Outraged by treason, the crown of Grand Duchy of Luwia mobilizes imperial cohorts to crush the upstart insurrection in People's Republic of Rabehodi. The Invasion of Rabehodi begins in fire and iron.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Ri'itqeuzeol stir mutiny among garrison troops in Chakab!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Clandestine agents from Lenonila sow suspicion in the frontier councils of Kilumopu.
QUEST COMPLETED: Recovery of the Raided Herd of Sano! Nemu returns the cattle and the clan sends 100 Gold!
TITAN CLASH: The armies of Nenubonape clash with The Radiant Sovereign in cell 262! The beast resists with 37/230 HP.

TITAN WRATH: Agitated by the eldritch sorcery, blasphemous iconoclasm, bloody societal chaos of Iyghezy, The Radiant Sovereign (Golden Sun Lion) stirs with ancient fury, embarking on a catastrophic rampage toward Iyghezy!

The Luna–Sa'ajek'in Rustline is rebuilt: Pejoku relays the track, and trains run again.
The Bizuwu–Reme Rustline of Wuberadata reaches Yemiradomu: a new station opens to cheering crowds (+trade).

Pilgrims of the Pilgrims of the Old Voice daub Wujnibabad in warning-sign sigils and drink only from irradiated springs.
The Pilgrims of the Old Voice gathers around a still-humming reactor ruin near Nopsum'u, praying to the glow.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Oyo-roka (Nenubonape).

A ritual flower war is fought between Chimwamhuacan and its neighbours; captives, not land, are the prize.

Roars of The Radiant Sovereign echo across the wilderness, striking fear into travelers and local herders.

Day of Rain Offerings: People of Nipi wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Nipi.
Canoe Launching: People of Kilumopu wake the year with song and fresh green boughs at Kilumopu.
Flames engulf the towers of Luna! Soldiers of Vuwo force the inner courtyards of No'ajaw's capital; the royal garrison breaks, and the seat of power falls.
Garrisons of Linosobebu storm the ramparts of Kilumopu, driving out the defenders of Lohyapy and hoisting their triumphant colors.
Night of the Veil: Families in Hywo set out lamps and food for their dead at Caer Bele.
The walls of Tikimoto crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Luwia breach the defenses of Rabehodi's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
Envoys from Te'axgyeh and Qeutzaagh exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Free Union of Wuberadata mobilizes its hosts against Grand Duchy of Luwia. Banners unfurl for the War of the Luwia Crown.
A victor's peace is forged: after 5 years of campaign in the Border War of Eytughy, Ze'olyat prevail, annexing contested borderlands.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Chimwamhuacan seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of No'ajaw! The people inaugurate the Free Union of Chimwamhuacan under the stewardship of Tlimwip.
Tlimwip is acclaimed ruler of Free Union of Chimwamhuacan.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Chommom seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of Lenonila! The people inaugurate the Commune of Chommom under the stewardship of Kalchich.
Kalchich is acclaimed ruler of Commune of Chommom.
Strange portents disturb the folk of Ukyutt: two-headed calves are born and springs run wine-dark. Priests offer fervent sacrifices.
Dust storms and blighted crops leave We'be on half-rations; canned stores are guarded at gunpoint.
The lords of We'be hoard grain and sell it dear; Ba'joi grows richer as the villages empty.
Wudlusa (Grand Champion) bestows glorious sporting renown upon the host realm in the international games in Sadfusabad.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Luwia storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Ronomi proclaims the foundation of the People's Republic of Luwia!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Hetytu strike at midnight in Vuwo! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the High Realm of Vuwo!
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Rutyhy! Nywe seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Stratocracy of Rutyhy!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Wenoki divert 20 gold from the tax vaults of Metlwintepec!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Wenoki are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Metlwintepec!

TITAN WRATH: Agitated by the eldritch sorcery, blasphemous iconoclasm, tyrannical depravity of Xu'ahuira, bloody societal chaos of Xu'artyth, The Emerald Qilin (Emerald Qilin) stirs with ancient fury, embarking on a catastrophic rampage toward Xu'artyth!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Pana pave the Ix-po'chu-Riwegemi Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Ix-po'chu and Riwegemi (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Qe'axliux pave the Qe'axliux-Reme Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Qe'axliux and Reme (+trade, +stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Zephyros the Sky-Sovereign hurls deafening thunderbolts across the frontiers of Bilad Baq, scattering hostile vanguards with righteous gales (+15% army power).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Nyxal the Void Dreamer projects psychic void-whispers into the foes of Nopsum'u! Invaders flee in weeping delirium, haunted by visions of tentacled cosmic voids (+18% army power, -7 stability).
DIVINE WRATH: Thalor the All-Seeing Mind clouds the counsel of Fumome! Arrogant scholars clash in bitter schisms, paralyzing governance (-10 stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Tzannik the Architect of Fate mutates the weave of fate in Chakab! Arcane mutations grant uncanny clairvoyance and secret gold, at the cost of civil panic (+30 gold, -6 stability).
RUINOUS GIFT: Luxuria the Gilded Prince intoxicates the high courts of So'chekab with exquisite hedonism! Opulence surges alongside reckless decadence (+40 gold, -10 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Gorath the Stone Peak heaves rich subterranean veins to the surface of Kilumopu! Granite ramparts harden against all siegecraft (+25 gold, +15 stability).

Scavengers of Momtetlmow overturn the cap-collectors’ carts when the canned stores run out.
Pima, bald and half-blind from the storms, preaches in Rulika that the sky will clear for those who stop digging.
Komtichpit, a lone courier, escorts a water convoy through the raider country to Chommom and refuses payment.

The court of Vuwo bans the Lantern Players of Tetymore; its masters flee across the border.
The peace dictated by O'irzaet ends thralldom in Bilad Baq; the victors impose manorial fiefs.
The peace dictated by Rulika ends clan commons in Kawmaltlan; the victors impose free citizenry.
Soldiers scatter a league of the low-born in Ragepe; Numikoku keeps guild castes by force.
A Golden Warmth spreads across Dekoru: vineyards climb north and the passes stay open all year.
The tiny Rift-Dominion of Rupe seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Nenubonape.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Rumar bars the shaft to Tiwchan, and the tithe-collectors of Vuwo are turned back at the lamps of Pejoku.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Qe'axliux bars the shaft to Qishqin, and the tithe-collectors of Lushyujdas are turned back at the lamps of Qe'axliux.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Loolruyx bars the shaft to Qasr Tub, and the tithe-collectors of Lohyapy are turned back at the lamps of Ze'olyat.
SKY BLOCKADE: the floating hosts of Al-wuh close the air-lanes above Ronavurea, starving Wuberadata of the high trade.
The Kawmaltlan–Rulika War is known as the Aggression among the Lelwetchak, and as the Vindication among the Pomome.
The Invasion of Bilad Baq is known as the Vindication among the I'olryoqheur, and as the Aggression among the Mumdabyil.
Nenubonape sends an expedition through the Burning Tear.
Envoys from Fipopenui and Chimwamhuacan exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Tlischala of Pammeywamtap turns from the old cause toward vengeance.
Dynastic extinction strikes Pammeywamtap: Tlischal dies heirless (fever). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Mitpatllan claims the vacant crown.
An epochal spiritual turning: the monarch and lords of Numowukawa embrace the Mother of Tenelu, casting aside former traditions.

AGRARIAN REVOLT: Crushed by feudal cap levies and noble exploitation, the laborers of Tetymore rise in open insurrection! Renouncing the lords of Numowukawa, they establish the People's Republic of Lyhe with Bara leading the commune.
Bara is acclaimed ruler of People's Republic of Lyhe.
Vowing to eradicate rebellion, Military Junta of Numowukawa marches swiftly upon People's Republic of Lyhe. The drums of the Hundred Days War of Lyhe echo across the provinces.
Nozako (Master Artificer) constructs a magnificent clockwork astrolabe atop the harbor watchtower in Redigo.
Te'arziyz (Master Artificer) engineers a revolutionary watermill mechanism that doubles grain milling yields in Xuetugg.

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Ri'itqeuzeol as a mass uprising topples the throne of High Realm of Ri'itqeuzeol! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Ti'jaka proclaims the sovereign Confederation of Ri'itqeuzeol!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Assassins from Nenubonape strike in the dead of night, slaying Huhe in the court of Tikimoto!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Figvar detonate powder stores in Takhtiy, gutting frontline regiments!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Figvar are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Takhtiy!
QUEST COMPLETED: Recovery of the Chant Staff of Wemuka! Nunengari brings the staff to the elders, who chant it whole again and reward the sacred relic Blood-gilded Circlet of Mukotadutu!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Kosone pave the Kosone-Sisekonu Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Kosone and Sisekonu (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Feba pave the Feba-Techmen Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Feba and Techmen (+trade, +stability).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Nyxal the Void Dreamer projects psychic void-whispers into the foes of Sidywy! Invaders flee in weeping delirium, haunted by visions of tentacled cosmic voids (+18% army power, -7 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Gorath the Stone Peak heaves rich subterranean veins to the surface of O'irzaet! Granite ramparts harden against all siegecraft (+25 gold, +15 stability).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Caer Riwaty! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
The vault-born Guteku clears the tunnels under Tisigumeru of mutant swarms; the people call them Warden.
Pilgrims of the Order of the Last Vault daub Sekonu in warning-sign sigils and drink only from irradiated springs.
Unrest of the year: bread riots in Hoizziiq (Ze'olyat).

Fires leap on rooftops of Ethuzy for the new-year spring; Lohyapy jumps the flames for luck.
The Linoro and Lelwetchak quarters of Feba have married so often that a new lineage, the house of Weltakodese, is spoken of; its latest child is Pechteta Weltakodese.
After years of agitation, religious tolerance is enacted in Metlwintepec; Melman Tokwan is cheered through the streets of Hokebu.
In Wantlan the Temperance Union gathers crowds behind Watlwata Chakwilchil, demanding temperance for Wantlan.
In Chu'jeha, a movement of free tenants takes root among the tenants, demanding an end to manorial fiefs.
Whispers in the fields of Pammeywamtap: the cause of emancipation gathers the bound spirits against bound spirits.
A great fungal bloom carpets the caverns of Ze'olziez around Qoyeh; spore-bread and lamp-moss for all.
Over 104 years the speech of Ruhengahu has drifted from the Pomome tongue; its people now call themselves the Rakofa.
The tiny Merchant League of Figvar seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Lohyapy.

We'tatun squeezes the shaft-tolls of Qishqin; the miners of Lushyujdas mutter beneath the stone.

The Counting: Scholars and singers of Qe'axliux compete in Qe'axliux; the best verse is carried through the streets.
The Numowukawa–Vegymore Rustline is cut: soldiers of Numikoku tear up the salvage rail track and the trains stop.
Fipopenui overruns the defensive holdfasts of Ho'uqhior, annexing the town and its fertile environs from Ze'olyat.
The banners of Numowukawa are raised over Yekezaki as victorious cohorts march in, ending Lyhe's dominion over the district.
Garrisons of Numowukawa storm the ramparts of Raseciluvuvy, driving out the defenders of Lyhe and hoisting their triumphant colors.
Ballgame Festival: Warriors of Kawmaltlan parade and wrestle in the squares of Kawmaltlan to honour the old victories.
The walls of Tetymore crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Numowukawa breach the defenses of Lyhe's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
The walls of Vegymore crumble under heavy assault! Cohorts of Numowukawa breach the defenses of Lyhe's capital, scattering the garrison and sacking the palace.
Envoys from Fipopenui and Taju exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of High Realm of Lofzamin proclaim war upon Merchant League of Takhtiy. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the War of Lofzamin begins.

Ambition stirs in the courts of Confederation of Papmil, which openly claims dominion over Merchant League of Rulika. The holdfast braces as the Papmil–Rulika War erupts. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Linosobebu rally to Rulika's side.

With swords drawn and ancient pacts invoked, Grand Duchy of Wuberadata marches against Trade Federation of Lokkactlan. The Border War of Lokkactlan begins. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Nenubonape rally to Lokkactlan's side.
Neither camp can break the front: envoys sign a mutual cessation of hostilities, ending the War of Lofzamin (less than a year) in an uneasy truce.
Chi'yiba of Chakab takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Dynastic extinction strikes Chakab: Yu'jo dies heirless (a wasting sickness). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Sa'pane claims the vacant crown.

MERCANTILE SECESSION: Wealthy patricians and merchant cartels in Momtetlmow rebel against royal tariffs! Declaring commercial independence from Lokkactlan, Kelnawpak establishes the Commercial Union of Powkach.
Kelnawpak is acclaimed ruler of Commercial Union of Powkach.
Seeking to restore imperial order by force, Trade Federation of Lokkactlan dispatches punitive legions to subdue Commercial Union of Powkach. The bitter War of Lokkactlan is underway.
Nozako (Master Artificer) invents an ingenious optical telescope to survey distant constellations in Redigo.
Ji'wepi (Master Artificer) invents an ingenious optical telescope to survey distant constellations in Che'wea.

COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Nunengari strike at midnight in Fipopenui! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Divine Realm of Fipopenui!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Crowds fill the avenues of Qasr Fatsiq as a mass uprising topples the throne of Kingdom of Qasr Fatsiq! The ancient autocracy is abolished, and Karbiqa proclaims the sovereign Free Commonwealth of Qasr Fatsiq!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Syre strike at midnight in Linosobebu! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Principality of Linosobebu!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Ze'olziez detonate powder stores in Nenubonape, gutting frontline regiments!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of O'irzaet are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Xu'artyth!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Duhar detonate powder stores in Luswuj, gutting frontline regiments!

OVER-FARMING DUST BOWL: Decades of intensive cultivation and overgrazing exhaust the arid topsoil around the hinterlands of Zawu. Violent dust storms sweep the plains, suffocating crops and forcing herders into exile.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Tikimoto pave the Hugawu-Dabfusbiwfas Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Hugawu and Dabfusbiwfas (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Wulivach pave the Wulivach-Riyxzaagh Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Wulivach and Riyxzaagh (+trade, +stability).

ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Nyxal the Void Dreamer projects psychic void-whispers into the foes of Sidywy! Invaders flee in weeping delirium, haunted by visions of tentacled cosmic voids (+18% army power, -7 stability).
NATURE BLESSING: Undina of the Silver Basin purifies the sacred rivers of Nenubonape! Abundant fish and unhindered river trade enrich the townships (+30 gold, +12 stability).
ELDRITCH WRATH: Shubbog the Brood Mother unleashes voracious dark young upon Mayliltlan! Abominations devour cattle and ravage boundary settlements (-15 stability, -20 gold).
ELDRITCH MANIFESTATION: Cthulor the Abyssal Slumberer stirs in the ocean abyss beneath Papmil! Barnacle-encrusted cyclopean monoliths surface, loaded with pre-human treasure (+35 gold, -5 stability).
PATRON MIRACLE: Omnipotis the Sovereign Architect manifests the Sovereign Mandate in Rutyhy! Incorruptible celestial magistrates codify sacred law, crushing unrest (+20 stability, +15 gold).
PATRON MIRACLE: Thalor the All-Seeing Mind whispers lost epics and architectural secrets to the scholars of Numowukawa, ushering in an era of enlightened innovation (+14 stability, +20 gold).

Mayliltlan crushes the cause of emancipation; its leaders hang and the bondsfolk are bound tighter.

monsters.name: Vermithrax Flameseeker
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: The Radiant Sovereign
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: The Great Calydonian Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: Behemoth the Earth-Shaker
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: Glacies the Glacial Drake
monsters.lore: A frost-breathing great wyrm dwelling in glacial crevasses, freezing rivers solid with a single exhalation.

monsters.name: The Dune-Shadow Roc
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: The Celestial Raptor
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: The Emerald Qilin
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: The River Kappa
monsters.lore: A water imp with a dish of water on its head; bow to it, and courtesy forces it to bow back and spill its strength.

monsters.name: The Black Cadejo

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards

people.name: Todbek
people.title: inventor
people.look: A lean-jawed figure with amber eyes, braided starlight hair and high pointed ears, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries a ticking clockwork gizmo and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Kewute
people.title: artist
people.look: A wiry figure with dark obsidian eyes, star-freckled skin and eyes like captured nebulae, and freckled skin and a wry half-smile. Carries charcoal-stained cuffs and a lute and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Liwe
people.title: K'uhul Ajaw of Muchekab
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with dark obsidian eyes, a faint solar halo and luminous gold-white hair, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a circlet of realm-gold and moves with a quiet, cat-like economy.

people.name: Kabyisa
people.title: prophet
people.look: A statuesque figure with deep violet eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and stern, deeply etched brow lines. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Piptisha
people.title: hero
people.look: A wiry figure with pale ice-blue eyes, braided starlight hair and high pointed ears, and a faded duelling scar across the cheek. Carries a polished buckler and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Iysulkiw
people.title: hero
people.look: A stocky figure with deep violet eyes, pearlescent scales along the temples and webbed ears, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a polished buckler and Tilts their head as if listening to distant music.

people.name: Sujshata
people.title: Sultan of Sakfahabad
people.look: A statuesque figure with slate-grey eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and a burn-mark from an old forge spark. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and speaks in measured, unhurried tones.

people.name: Yishway
people.title: Sultan of Muznim
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with pale ice-blue eyes, desiccated royal wrappings and a gilded death-mask, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a signet ring of state and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Lihbuycadi
people.title: Maharaja of Finzten
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with amber eyes, raven hair pinned with leaf-filigree, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries a signet ring of state and watches every doorway with restless eyes.

people.name: Yashduti
people.title: thinker
people.look: A stocky figure with hazel eyes, raven hair pinned with leaf-filigree, and a tattoo of a coiled serpent on the wrist. Carries an astrolabe and ink-horn and gestures animatedly while speaking.

people.name: Wenitino
people.title: prophet
people.look: A compact and muscular figure with bright gold eyes, curved horn-bosses and a bristling mane, and sun-creased eyes and a steady gaze. Carries a staff hung with scripture-strips and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

people.name: Tamlasha
people.title: Sultan of Diveshu
people.look: A tall and gaunt figure with copper-flecked eyes, parchment skin, sunken sockets alight with cold blue fire, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries an orb-pommelled ceremonial blade and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Liduvi
people.title: prophet
people.look: A sinewy figure with deep violet eyes, pale astral locks and obsidian-ringed eyes, and ritual ash-marks along the brow. Carries a tablet of prophecies and laughs easily but keeps a hand near the belt.

people.name: Ripetewo
people.title: prophet
people.look: A lithe figure with amber eyes, amber feline slit-eyes and a striped mane, and a braided jawline and wind-chapped skin. Carries ash-streaked robes and a铜 bell and carries themselves with rigid military posture.

events.text: The tiny Popular Commonwealth of Rapnarkot seeks shelter and is peacefully absorbed into Meyrut.
Finzten squeezes the shaft-tolls of Botonebo; the miners of Wolemi mutter beneath the stone.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Ka-keso bars the shaft to Munelura, and the tithe-collectors of Wolemi are turned back at the lamps of Wage.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Ka-gago bars the shaft to Munelura, and the tithe-collectors of Wolemi are turned back at the lamps of Keoryth.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Kijatokab bars the shaft to Pridro, and the tithe-collectors of Rupe are turned back at the lamps of Diveshu.
Diveshu squeezes the shaft-tolls of Yojotun; the miners of Sabase mutter beneath the stone.
A twisting storm drops from a green sky onto Kikazuwa, tearing a mile-long scar through houses and barns.
Lightning sets the dry woods of Finzten alight; the fire runs to the edge of Shipyel before the rains come.
The War of Diveshu is known as the Liberation among the Tenu, and as the Betrayal among the Lepelo.
Finzten overruns the defensive holdfasts of Yehres, annexing the town and its fertile environs from Nishcit.
Ninsik's invasion through the Silent Wound into Zotbozdiv was repulsed at Meldar.
Festival of the New Count: The longest night in Yitekab is spent by firelight in Yitekab, with stories and gifts.
Garrisons of Finzten storm the ramparts of Choslow, driving out the defenders of Nishcit and hoisting their triumphant colors.
After a bitter siege, the ramparts of Nishcit give way! Vanguard forces of Finzten storm the royal seat of Nishcit, casting down imperial banners and plundering the state vaults.
The banners of Po'chu are raised over Ngati as victorious cohorts march in, ending Panga's dominion over the district.
Games of the Arena: Warriors of Prapre parade and wrestle in the squares of Tracrium to honour the old victories.
Envoys from Nuja and Po'chu exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Wokafa of Sati takes up the cause of the safety of the holdfast.
The death of Sofobipi Matu (a hunting accident) leaves Sati without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Mupawu seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.
Lida of Nuqu takes up the cause of the fortunes of the dynasty.
Dynastic extinction strikes Nuqu: Sataba dies heirless (a fall from a horse). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Dani claims the vacant crown.
Artificers and scholars achieve a historic breakthrough: Reactor Revival (Compact Magnetic Torus, Dyson Collector Swarm) spreads between guilds and academies across the realms!
Philosopher Susvuzhvag of Morgiy achieves worldwide acclaim with their magnum opus: "Dialogue on the Motion of Spheres".
Ese (Grand Champion) sets an unprecedented record in the sprint and javelin throwing trials in Bijumi.
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Sero storm the government palace in Wage! The faction seizes control, establishing the Principality of Wage.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Rupe divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Newa!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Yehgavpura divert 23 gold from the tax vaults of Drecrium!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Chakanal divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Rupe!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Chakanal are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Rupe!
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Nuja pave the Julu-Critla Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Julu and Critla (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Nishcit pave the Sompaskab-Gaphish Royal Road, establishing a direct route between Sompaskab and Gaphish (+trade, +stability).

DIVINE PROXY WAR: The war between Nishcit and Wolemi escalates into a celestial proxy duel! Omnipotis the Sovereign Architect rallies the hosts of Nishcit, while Gorath the Stone Peak unleashes sacred omens to shield Wolemi.

DIVINE PROXY WAR: The war between Blodro and Nuqu escalates into a celestial proxy duel! Ignis the Hearth Caldera rallies the hosts of Blodro, while Sylvanor the Forest Horn unleashes sacred omens to shield Nuqu.
NATURE BLESSING: Ignis the Hearth Caldera stokes the caldera hearths of Meyrut! Master smiths forge shimmering obsidian weaponry bathed in magma (+16% army power, +15 gold).
NATURE BLESSING: Ignis the Hearth Caldera stokes the caldera hearths of Blodro! Master smiths forge shimmering obsidian weaponry bathed in magma (+16% army power, +15 gold).
NATURE BLESSING: Sylvanor the Forest Horn awakens the ancient canopies of Ka-fupo! Verdant thickets ensnare enemies and provide abundant woodland forage (+16 stability, +10% army power).
The vault-born Tafzhora clears the tunnels under Duhzgiyfakh of mutant swarms; the people call them Warden.
The vault-born Shuvaka clears the tunnels under Dicinagar of mutant swarms; the people call them Warden.
Pilgrims of the Pilgrims of the Old Voice daub Cha'enal in warning-sign sigils and drink only from irradiated springs.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Badudathani (Meyrut).

Sero of Wage comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Powufa conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Ashen Labyrinth) using tactic (score 29 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Koro survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 7 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red. Salvaged ancient relic: Sun Stone Shard!
Astronomers of Ajoleba predict the eclipse to the day; Ajoleba celebrates the turning of a great cycle.
Games fill the arena of Drecrium; Plonlana feasts for a week in honour of its founding.
The last patron of the Wandering School of Vlofro turns on it: Sloqli burns its works and silences the masters.
By decree, Munelura ends manorial fiefs. Bells ring in Gekoso as the holdfast adopts free guilds.
Delvers of Plonlana break into a hall of glowing crystals; the deep realm grows.
TAX REVOLT: the undercity of Ka-gago bars the shaft to Munelura, and the tithe-collectors of Wolemi are turned back at the lamps of Keoryth.
Wolemi squeezes the shaft-tolls of Gekoso; the miners of Munelura mutter beneath the stone.
The earth heaves along the Qahila Trench: a magnitude 7.7 quake splits the streets of Ngati, and fires follow the falling roofs.
After the quake on the Qahila Trench a great wave strikes the coast: harbours from Ngati along the shore are smashed and the fields drowned in salt.
Hunger follows ruin: with fields lost, famine spreads across Po'chu.
Ma'pe opens the royal canned stores of Po'chu; bread is carted to every village and the people bless the crown.
The spring flood of the Gepyow is the worst in living memory: Tisthani is cut off for a month.
WILDFIRE: In the dry heat at summer’s end the forests around Vutlan catch fire; smoke hangs over Meyrut for weeks.
The banners of Finzten are raised over Shudpatna as victorious cohorts march in, ending Nishcit's dominion over the district.
Griots’ Epic Nights: Scholars and singers of Dulokura compete in Dulokura; the best verse is carried through the streets.
Flames engulf the towers of Sompaskab! Soldiers of Finzten force the inner courtyards of Nishcit's capital; the royal garrison breaks, and the seat of power falls.
The banners of Po'chu are raised over Toholu as victorious cohorts march in, ending Panga's dominion over the district.
Following fierce fighting along the fortifications, Rahingahu surrenders to Po'chu; its magistrates swear fealty as Panga's banner is hauled down.
Envoys from Toviruni and Sati exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of Democratic Union of Vaydid proclaim war upon Principality of Panga. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the War of Vaydid begins.

Ambition stirs in the courts of Artificer Directorate of Newa, which openly claims dominion over Commune of Riba. The holdfast braces as the Hundred Days War of Riba erupts. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Munelura rally to Riba's side.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Ninsik Succession War ends in mutual exhaustion after 2 years; borders return to former lines.
Dutuma of Lihuba takes up the cause of wealth.
Dynastic extinction strikes Lihuba: Dabima dies heirless (old age). Amid whispers of poison and sword-drawn councils, House Hunifahu claims the vacant crown.
Nurage of Newa takes up the cause of a lasting legacy.
The death of Dawusa Rugokimoluru (a wasting sickness) leaves Newa without an acknowledged heir. In the ensuing succession crisis, House Lisiku seizes the high throne amidst palace turmoil.
Artificers and scholars achieve a historic breakthrough: Coherent Particle Arrays (High-Power Optical Maser, Superconducting Railgun) spreads between guilds and academies across the realms!
Kewute (Master Artisan) completes a cathedral ceiling fresco celebrating the history of the holdfast in Juchitun.

CONSTITUTIONAL REFORM: The Grand Assembly of Sabase peacefully promulgates a new constitutional charter! Yielding absolute authority, Tocho transitions Principality of Sabase into the Council of Ingenuity of Sabase.

STATE ATHEISM PROCLAIMED: The revolutionary leadership in Sabase enacts Radical Secularization! State religion is abolished, temple estates and monastery vaults are confiscated for the people (+65 gold), and ancient dogma is suppressed.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Shadow agents from Wubtud divert 25 gold from the tax vaults of Lukewefe!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Agitators dispatched by Lukewefe stir mutiny among garrison troops in Lijazabad!

QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Wurwaysima embarks upon the Rescue of the Lost Caravan Near Nekin! Wurwaysima hears that a pilgrim caravan has missed its well and is overdue near Nekin.

The Great Ajoleba War reaches its conclusion after 1 year of bloodshed: Ajoleba triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.

The final citadels fall, and the crown of Iron Dominion of Peboba is broken forever. With treasuries emptied and borders dissolved, Resuka Kudufupelopi flees into bitter exile as the holdfast fades into legend.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the Finzten–Peboba War after less than a year. With frontiers redrawn, Finzten & Yehgavpura dictate terms to the vanquished.
White banners flutter over the war camps. The Nginggen Campaign ends in mutual exhaustion after 2 years; borders return to former lines.
Feast of the Harvest Drums: Granaries of Munelura are opened at Gekoso; the whole town eats until dusk.
Ballgame of the Hero Twins: Warriors of Sabase parade and wrestle in the squares of Cha'enal to honour the old victories.
Envoys from Po'chu and Sitpura exchange solemn vows of mutual defense, binding their courts in a grand alliance.
Citing border encroachments and bitter territorial grievances, Protectorate of Nuja mobilizes its hosts against United Provinces of Plollotro. Banners unfurl for the Invasion of Plollotro.

Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Grand Marshalate of Sitpura launches a determined invasion into Principality of Nginggen, igniting the Invasion of Nginggen. Pledging mutual defense, the levies of Meyrut rally to Nginggen's side.
Exhausted by protracted attrition, both sides sign an armistice concluding the Ngawsim Campaign (1 year). Scabbards are sheathed and the status quo ante is restored.
Defying the crown of Finzten, the garrison and civic guilds of Mufoba mutiny! The sovereign Grand Marshalate of Mufoba is declared with Kesa at its helm.
Kesa is acclaimed ruler of Grand Marshalate of Mufoba.

The Nojewi–Newa War is known as the Vindication among the Lepelo, and as the Aggression among the Nguronisipu.
Flames engulf the towers of Lesecigarh! Soldiers of Citipura force the inner courtyards of Lesecigarh's capital; the royal garrison breaks, and the seat of power falls.
An ancient sovereign power falls to dust: Trade Federation of Lesecigarh is extinguished. Royal archives smolder, and Ditake Mida flees into obscurity.
The Conquest of Lesecigarh reaches its conclusion after 3 years of bloodshed: Citipura triumph decisively, forcing a humiliating treaty upon their foes.
The banners of Finzten are raised over Sikab as victorious cohorts march in, ending Ninsik's dominion over the district.
A catastrophic blow to Pongayu: legions of Nerine overrun the citadel of Pongayu, seizing the royal seat and routing the high council.
Banners trampled and throne abandoned, Commercial Union of Pongayu ceases to exist as a sovereign power. Tema Morogutaro flees the ashes of their former dominion.
Envoys convene upon neutral ground to ratify a solemn treaty, concluding the War of the Pongayu Crown after less than a year. With frontiers redrawn, Nerine dictate terms to the vanquished.
After 47 months, the Swollen Death is gone; Ninsik counts the empty houses.
Denouncing ancient covenants, the heralds of Grand Duchy of Rupe proclaim war upon Scavenger Compact of Wubtud. Trumpets sound across the frontier as the Wubtud Succession War begins.
Old border feuds boil over into open bloodshed: Democratic Union of Blodro launches a determined invasion into Free Trading Cities of Lihuba, igniting the Blodro–Lihuba War.
A victor's peace is forged: after 7 years of campaign in the Nojewi–Newa War, Nojewi prevail, annexing contested borderlands.
Neither camp can break the front: envoys sign a mutual cessation of hostilities, ending the Hundred Days War of Toviruni (1 year) in an uneasy truce.
Wuna of Nenubonape Beyond takes up the cause of wealth.
A perilous interregnum grips Nenubonape Beyond following the heirless death of Raga (old age). Retainers of House Yanodumopoko storm the assembly and usurp the crown.

POPULAR UPRISING: Folk moots and agrarian communes in Critla seize local canned stores and cast off the yoke of Nuja! The people inaugurate the Workers' Federation of Critla under the stewardship of Clokhro.
Clokhro is acclaimed ruler of Workers' Federation of Critla.
The civic bell of Bachenal tolls as magistrates and clan heads inaugurate the Chiefdom of Sabapo, establishing its seat of power.
Clean rain falls on Toviruni for a full season: crops root, trade convoys multiply and the old reactors finally cool.
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Nerine! Topo seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Syndicate of Nerine!
COUP D'ETAT: Mutinous conspirators led by Tamlasha strike at midnight in Diveshu! The revolutionary council seizes control, overthrowing the sovereign and proclaiming the Grand Duchy of Diveshu!

POPULAR REVOLUTION: Rising against tyranny and privilege, the populace of Tozingo storms the seat of government! With the former regime swept aside, Revuke proclaims the foundation of the United Provinces of Tozingo!
COUP D'ETAT: A sudden palace putsch overthrows the established order in Lelafo! Dewowa seizes control amidst martial decrees, proclaiming the Grand Duchy of Lelafo!
COUP D'ETAT: Armed regiments loyal to Zaduha storm the government palace in Lukewefe! The faction seizes control, establishing the Cybernetic Union of Lukewefe.
COVERT INTRIGUE: Covert saboteurs from Wage detonate powder stores in Kete, gutting frontline regiments!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Wage are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Kete!
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Goleke are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Po'chu!
COVERT INTRIGUE: Clandestine agents from Meygap sow suspicion in the frontier councils of Rupe.
DIPLOMATIC SCANDAL: Envoys of Meygap are expelled after their covert spies are unmasked in Rupe!
QUEST COMPLETED: Repairing the Broken Aqueduct of Drecrentum! Blilra sees the water flow into the city fountains, and the senate decrees Immortal Renown and a steadier realm!
QUEST UNDERTAKEN: Yisshaj embarks upon the Raid on the Shadow Keep in Shinsan! Yisshaj gathers scouts and infiltrates the frontier redoubts near Shinsan to pinpoint the captive's cell.
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Munelura pave the Gekoso-Shudpatna Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Gekoso and Shudpatna (+trade, +stability).
NEW HIGHWAY: Engineers of Neriganagara pave the Neriganagara-Gupo Silk Highway, establishing a direct route between Neriganagara and Gupo (+trade, +stability).
Salvage crews of Noybsak sabotage the recruiters’ trucks rather than serve.
Nigngoh, a lone courier, escorts a water convoy through the raider country to Tisthani and refuses payment.
Pilgrims of the Pilgrims of the Old Voice daub Chanokab in warning-sign sigils and drink only from irradiated springs.
The vault-born Cholati clears the tunnels under Ajoleba of mutant swarms; the people call them Warden.
Pilgrims of the Rust Chorus daub LoozR' in warning-sign sigils and drink only from irradiated springs.
Unrest of the year: tax riots in Tuhkot (Meyrut); bread riots in Sompaskab (Ninsik).

Topo of Nerine comes to the throne bent on wealth.
Topo of Nerine fills the treasury, the wealth long sought.
Tamlasha of Diveshu comes to the throne bent on knowledge.
Revuke of Tozingo comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Dewowa of Lelafo comes to the throne bent on the fortunes of the dynasty.
Zaduha of Lukewefe comes to the throne bent on the spread of the faith.
Kodofovo of Dudafukibe secures the line, with Reba grown to take the crown.
Lipluta conquered Floor 1 (Floor of the Ashen Labyrinth) using assault (score 32 vs DC 8). Defeated Oryx. Promoted to F-Rank!
Cihtish survived descent to Layer 1 (Edge of the Abyss), enduring 8 strain damage: Light dizziness and loss of balance upon ascent. Whistle tier: red.
Critla completes a great aqueduct at Critla, a marvel of the Brotre people.
Ngoseba of Newa outlaws a league of the low-born. The lay castes fall silent, for now.
Whispers in the fields of Tasshuknim: a league of the landless gathers the tenants against manorial fiefs.
A cave-in thunders through Relodugu; Wolemi digs for survivors for weeks.
A warm current sweeps past Buhebo; shoals of silver fish and drifting pearls enrich Tohakonegara.

monsters.name: Titan of the Steppes
monsters.lore: A colossal terrestrial colossus whose bones are tubes of bronze and limbs like bars of iron, roaming ancient grasslands.

monsters.name: Lion of the Golden Dawn
monsters.lore: An immortal noble lion with a mane of radiant sunlight, whose majestic roar dispels dark enchantments.
monsters.trophy: Solar Lion Mane of Golden Light

monsters.name: Vermithrax Flameseeker
monsters.lore: An ancient volcanic dragon sleeping atop mountains of melted gold, reducing invading armies to calcined bones.

monsters.name: Ziz the Storm-Sovereign
monsters.lore: A colossal winged terror of celestial heights whose wingspan eclipses the noon sun and commands cyclones.

monsters.name: Shadow of the Loch
monsters.lore: An elusive plesiosaur-like lake cryptid spoken of in local campfire folklore, surfacing only when mists veil the waters.

monsters.name: Roc the Sky-Render
monsters.lore: The roc of sailors' and caravaneers' tall tales, a bird vast enough to carry off an elephant; its wingbeats raise dust storms over the canyons.

monsters.name: Iron-Hide Boar
monsters.lore: A massive armored tusker leading wild forest herds, tearing up farmland and trampling watchtowers.
monsters.trophy: Calydonian Boar Great Tusks & Armored Hide

monsters.name: The Auspicious Horned Beast
monsters.lore: A gentle horned dragon-beast cloaked in scales of jade, appearing only during the reigns of benevolent and enlightened rulers.

monsters.name: The Black Cadejo
monsters.lore: Spectral dogs of the night roads: the white one guards travellers, the black one leads them astray.

monsters.name: The River Ninki Nanka
monsters.lore: A dragon of the mangrove swamps; it is said that to see it is to fall ill.

monsters.name: The Ponaturi of the Reef
monsters.lore: Hostile sea goblins of the old hero tales who sleep beneath the waves by day and come ashore at night; sunlight destroys them.

monsters.name: The Timingila of the Deep
monsters.lore: A sea monster of the old epics so vast it swallows whales whole, and is itself swallowed by something larger still.

species.name: Human
species.desc: Versatile and ambitious mortals who build sprawling empires across every continent.

species.name: Elf
species.desc: Graceful, long-lived beings attuned to primal magic, ancient forests, and stellar harmonies.

species.name: Dwarf
species.desc: Stout, resolute masters of masonry, deep mining, and forged steel who carve citadels into living stone.

species.name: Orc
species.desc: Fierce, muscular warriors governed by martial honor, blood covenants, and relentless resilience.

species.name: Troll
species.desc: Massive, regenerative brutes of mossy crags and deep wetlands possessing primeval strength.

species.name: Beastman
species.desc: Prideful therianthropic folk bearing lupine, feline, or minotaur aspects, hunters of boundless wildlands.

species.name: Halfling
species.desc: Clever, jovial, and nimble folk who build peaceful pastoral burrows or intricate clockwork workshops.

species.name: Giant
species.desc: Colossal beings of primeval stone, frost, and storm, keeping ancient memory of the world's dawn.

species.name: Goblin
species.desc: Prolific, cunning, and resourceful tinkerers who thrive in shadowy crevices, mines, and scrap cities.

species.name: Dragonborn
species.desc: Scale-bound noble warriors descended from dragons, wielding elemental breath and stubborn pride.

species.name: Merfolk
species.desc: Aquatic humanoids of the coral reefs and sunlit shallows, rulers of the pelagic depths.

species.name: Starborn
species.desc: Luminous beings born of falling stars and astral conduits, radiating transcendent grace.

species.name: Ratfolk
species.desc: Cunning subterranean rodentkin and warpstone tinkerers who breed rapidly in foul under-empires.

species.name: Lizardfolk
species.desc: Cold-blooded ancient guardians of the geomantic web who defend temple-cities under primal mandates.

species.name: Tomb Revenant
species.desc: Ancient slumbering skeletal pharaohs and living-metal monarchs commanding eternal legions.

species.name: Ogor
species.desc: Massive nomadic brute warriors driven by eternal hunger and gut-magic across mountains and steppes.

species.name: Void Elf
species.desc: Ancient psychic wanderers of cosmic webways with spirit stones preserving souls against the void.

species.name: Warp Fiend
species.desc: Horned warp-manifestations born of cosmic fractures and excess emotion hungry for slaughter.

species.name: Chitin Swarm
species.desc: Synaptic bio-constructs with chittering carapaces driven by a devouring hive-mind.

diseases.name: plague
diseases.desc: carried by fleas on rats and on the cloth of traders; it rides the roads and the ships

diseases.name: flux
diseases.desc: drunk from fouled wells and river water; it follows the rivers downstream and haunts the ports

diseases.name: pox
diseases.desc: passed hand to hand and breath to breath; those who live through it never take it again

diseases.name: marsh fever
symptoms: a yellow cast to the skin
diseases.desc: brought by biting flies in hot wetlands; it lingers where the water stands still

diseases.name: consumption
symptoms: a cough that brings up blood
diseases.desc: a slow sickness of crowded cities that eats the lungs over years

diseases.name: blight
diseases.desc: a rot of the crops, not of people: it kills by hunger

diseases.name: miasma
symptoms: a lead taste in the mouth
diseases.desc: the bad air of the factory towns, thickest where the chimneys stand closest

diseases.name: radiation sickness
diseases.desc: not caught but soaked up: it clings to fallout grounds and the dust of old craters

diseases.name: engineered strain
diseases.desc: something made in a vat or a lab that got out; it spreads fast and burns out fast

diseases.name: hollowing
symptoms: a cold that no fire warms
diseases.desc: a sickness of the spirit; the old wives say it comes from broken wards
